prose.heading: Why a photo booth earns its place at a wedding
paragraphs: Your photographer captures the day. A photo booth captures what your guests did with it — the table of cousins who piled in six at a time, the uncle who found the boa, the friends who came back four times over the night. Those are different photographs, and you generally only get them if there is a booth in the room.

There is also a practical argument. A booth keeps the room busy during the flat spots — the gap between dinner and dancing, the stretch while the band changes over — and it gives the guests who do not dance somewhere to be. Couples routinely tell us their guests stayed later than they expected, and the booth is usually part of why.

prose.heading: When to open the booth during your reception
paragraphs: Most weddings book three to four hours of booth time. The sweet spot is opening as cocktail hour ends and running through the heart of the dance floor, so the booth is live while the energy is highest rather than sitting idle through dinner speeches.

If your reception runs long, it is usually better to start the booth later than to start it early and have it close before the night peaks. We will talk this through with you when we quote rather than just selling you more hours.

prose.heading: Which booth suits a wedding
paragraphs: The mirror booth is the most-booked for weddings, because the full-length format handles whole wedding parties and works for every age in the room. The glam booth is the choice for black-tie weddings where you want the photos to look as considered as the outfits. The 360 booth is increasingly popular for younger crowds who will share the clip that night.
For guest lists over about 150, we often suggest pairing a static booth with the roaming attendant so the seated tables get covered too and nobody spends the evening in a queue.

prose.heading: What your venue will need from us
paragraphs: Most wedding venues ask for a certificate of insurance naming them as additionally insured. We carry a $3 million policy and turn COIs around the same day you send us the venue contact — worth knowing if you have already chased another vendor for one.

On the day we arrive an hour before your start time and set up in about 20 minutes. We need a 10ft x 10ft space ideally, 8ft x 8ft at minimum, and a standard outlet within 15 feet that is not shared with the DJ or catering.

recHeading: The three booths couples book most
recSub: Any of them will work at a wedding. These are the ones that work best, and why.

prose.heading: What a photo booth does for a corporate event
paragraphs: At an internal event — a holiday party, a summer outing, an awards night — the booth does the social work. It gives people who do not know each other a reason to stand together, and it produces something they take home. That is a different outcome from a photographer circulating the room.

At an external event — a launch, a trade show stand, a brand activation — the booth is a marketing channel. Every photo that leaves carries your branding, shared by the attendee to an audience that trusts them. It is distribution you cannot buy directly.

prose.heading: Branding the whole experience
paragraphs: We can wrap the booth entirely in your colors, build a custom start screen, apply branded photo overlays, print custom backdrops, and host the images in a branded online gallery or microsite. Consistency matters here — a generic booth in the middle of a carefully branded activation undermines the rest of the spend.
For a full physical wrap we need two to three weeks' notice so graphics can be printed and applied. Digital-only branding turns around considerably faster if your timeline is tight.

prose.heading: Capturing data, not just photos
paragraphs: Surveys and questionnaires can be built directly into the booth flow, so you collect product feedback at the moment attendees are most engaged rather than by email a week later. Opt-in contact capture builds a compliant list for remarketing, and we hand over a report of what was gathered.
The result is an activation you can put numbers against — engagement volume, opt-in rate, shares — rather than one you can only describe.

prose.heading: Working around corporate venue logistics
paragraphs: Midtown offices, hotel ballrooms, convention centers and gallery spaces all come with loading dock windows, freight elevator bookings, building engineers and COI requirements. We handle that paperwork as a matter of course and plan the load-in around your venue's actual access rather than the floor plan.
For multi-day trade shows, the roaming booth is often the better answer than a static one — it covers a stand where footfall is spread across a day rather than concentrated in an evening.

prose.heading: The party booth, and why the attendant matters most
paragraphs: Birthdays, Sweet Sixteens, bar and bat mitzvahs, quinceañeras, graduations, showers, reunions and retirements — the booth does the same job at all of them. It gives guests something to do together, and it sends everyone home with a photo instead of a party favour they will throw away.

The variable that decides whether it works is the attendant. Left alone, a booth gets a flurry of use and then sits quiet. Staffed properly, someone is starting lines, restocking props, handing prints over and pulling in the people standing at the edges. That person is included in every rental we do.

prose.heading: Choosing a booth for a younger crowd
paragraphs: For Sweet Sixteens, mitzvahs and proms, the 360 booth is usually the right call. That crowd is going to post the clip before the night ends, which is exactly what a 360 produces. The Vogue booth is the other strong option — the LED interior looks dramatic in a dark room and renders a shareable video in about ten seconds.

For mixed-age parties — a milestone birthday, an anniversary, a family reunion — the mirror booth is the safer choice, because it is intuitive for guests who have never used one and roomy enough for a whole table to pile in.

prose.heading: What we need from your venue
paragraphs: Optimal setup is 10ft x 10ft with 7.5ft of ceiling clearance, which leaves room for the backdrop and props table. We can compress to 8ft x 8ft where space is tight. We need a standard 110V, 5-amp outlet within 15 feet, ideally on its own circuit rather than shared with the DJ.

If you are hosting at home rather than a venue, that is completely normal for us — a garden, a basement, a living room with the furniture moved. Just tell us what the space is really like and we will tell you honestly whether it fits.
